the effects of defoliation at the level of the individual cell.
the effect of defolation on leaf elongation and on the spatial pattern of cell expansion and production in perennial ryegrass.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduction in LER following defoliation is associated with a decrease in cell production and expansion.

the effect of defoliating perennial ryegrass on the growth and cell expansion processes in the leaf growth region can be described as an inhibition of cell division, a reduction in cell expansion, an inhibition of leaf cell production and a reduced final cell size.
the initial, non steady growth phase following defolation was characterized by a reduced cell expansion and a reduced production of cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LER decreased after defoliation because of reduced cell production rate, reduced cell final size, reduced expansion rate of cells at intermediate stages of growth and reduced growth zone length.
defoliation reduced LER by decreasing cell division, cell expansion, and the length of the growth zone, and that these effects were not compensated for by a reduced cell size at 14 d.

cell growth analysis during the initial, transient growth phase following defolation provides a more detailed and comprehensive understanding of the effect of defolaiton on LER.
